To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) dietary lipids influence the course of experimental tumors in a way that is dependent on the type of tumor, (2) the influence of dietary lipids on tumor growth depends upon the stage of the disease at which dietary lipids are administered, (3) dietary lipids affect the development of metastases, (4) dietary lipids may alter the immune response, and (5) dietary lipids can alter the course of an infectious disease.
dietary fat influences immune functions, that infectious diseases influence lipid metabolism, and that infectious diseases may alter the effects of dietary fat on immune functions.
the immune functions of mice fed high levels of fat were suppressed and the functions of mice fed low levels of fat were enhanced.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of dietary lipids upon the immune response, the development of cancer, and the metabolism of lipids in animals and humans.

the following: (1) the effects of dietary lipids upon fat metabolism, (2) the effects of infectious diseases upon fat metabolism and the immune response, (3) the effects of fat metabolism upon the immune response, and (4) the effects of immunosuppressive and immunostimulating agents upon fat metabolism and immunity.
the effects of infectious diseases on lipid metabolism and immune functions and their possible relationship to cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship between dietary fat intake, immunological competence and cancer is not well understood, that the available data are contradictory and that further research is needed.
the relationship between dietary lipids, immune functions and infectious disease is a complicated one.
infectious diseases, particularly those of viral origin, can influence the development of cancer by altering lipid metabolism as well by affecting the immune system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary lipids may influence the course of an infectious disease, the immune system, and cancer.
the immune system is a major target of infectious diseases and that infectious diseases can be a major cause of immunodeficiency.
the infectious disease, in addition to its effect on lipid metabolism, may influence immune functions and thus the outcome of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system is very sensitive to changes in dietary fat.
we have a lot to learn about how the immune system interacts with the body’s fat stores.
the immune response to a pathogen is not a static process.
